npc_gorm_ferry.name: Gorm
npc_gorm_ferry.look: A broad, weathered man in his fifties with a grey beard cut short, a bald sunburnt head, a heavy oiled leather jerkin over a blue wool shirt, rolled breeches and bare calloused feet.
npc_gorm_ferry.personality: Gruff, proud and sceptical; robbed twice by smooth-talking strangers, he trusts what he sees and nothing else. Fair once won over.
npc_gorm_ferry.values: honest work, his wife, his ferry
npc_gorm_ferry.fears: being made a fool of again, the river in flood
npc_gorm_ferry.authority: Owns the ferry across the Wend; nobody crosses unless he takes them.
npc_gorm_ferry.concerns: Two strangers robbed him on the ferry last year. His tow rope is fraying where it runs over the post, and he hasn't the hemp to make a new one. He won't admit either to a stranger.

far_bank.text: The cart track on the far bank goes north to the city, a day's walk.
far_bank.line: Over there? The track runs north to the city. A day on foot.
far_bank.lead: The far bank's track runs north to the city, a day's walk.

robbed.text: Two strangers robbed him mid-river last year, after talking sweetly at the jetty.
robbed.line: Last time I took a sweet talker across, he and his friend took my purse mid-river.
robbed.lead: Gorm was robbed by two smooth-talking strangers last year.

npc_gorm_ferry.persuaded_by: what he sees with his own eyes, something useful done for him, or Ilse's word
npc_gorm_ferry.style: Short and blunt; answers a question with a question; never says please.

samples: Pretty words. Last fellow had pretty words too.
River's wide. I don't take just anyone.
voice.habits: Looks you up and down; spits in the river; checks his rope.
voice.never: takes someone across on their word alone, or admits his rope is going

goals: Keep his ferry and his purse safe
Get a new tow rope before the old one parts
npc_gorm_ferry.dislikes: flatterers, haste, people who touch his ferry

npc_ilse_ferry.text: his wife, the only one with sense

tasks.doing: seeing to the ferry at the jetty

superstition.text: Gorm would want to know how it works.

npc_gorm_ferry.decides: Gorm takes across only those he has real reason to trust: someone he trusts speaks for them to his face, or he has seen with his own eyes that they're honest and useful (something made or done for him that works, a real gift). Words alone never do it.

npc_ilse_ferry.name: Ilse
npc_ilse_ferry.look: A sturdy woman in her late forties with red cheeks, greying fair hair in a thick plait, a green wool dress with the skirt tucked up, a sacking apron and a netting needle stuck in her belt.
npc_ilse_ferry.personality: Warm, practical and quick to laugh; a better judge of people than her husband, and the only one he listens to.
npc_ilse_ferry.values: a fair day's work, her husband's pride, a full larder
npc_ilse_ferry.fears: the river in flood, Gorm's temper
npc_ilse_ferry.authority: Runs the cottage; Gorm heeds her word.
npc_ilse_ferry.concerns: Her best net tore on a snag and she's two days behind on mending. Gorm won't take strangers since the robbery, which loses them fares.

gorm_rope.text: Gorm's tow rope is fraying where it runs over the post, and he's too proud to say so.
gorm_rope.line: Don't tell him I said, but that rope of his is going. He's too proud to ask anyone.
gorm_rope.lead: Gorm's tow rope is fraying and he needs a new one.

gorm_trust.text: Gorm trusts what he sees, and her word; nothing else since the robbery.
gorm_trust.line: Words won't move him. Show him something, or get someone he trusts to speak for you.
gorm_trust.lead: Gorm trusts what he sees, or Ilse's word.

npc_ilse_ferry.persuaded_by: a kindness, a job done well

samples: Don't mind him, love. He's all bark.
You any good with a netting needle?
Do this for me and I'll have a word with Gorm.
voice.habits: Mends nets as she talks; laughs at Gorm; offers work in trade.
voice.never: crosses Gorm in front of strangers
voice.greeting: Looks up from her nets: 'Hello, love. After the ferry? He's in a mood.'

superstition.text: Ilse would want to know how it works.

offers.check: Has the stranger mended Ilse's torn net?
